request.spec:
A claim that is moved to another person now receives the next number in the sequence it would be
numbered in (the sheet's, or its period's when per-period numbering is on), and its old number is
never used again; a draft, having no number, gets none. CLAIM_REASSIGNED carries the new number.
Moving claims together follows the same rule, in list order.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim that is moved to another person now receives the next number in the sequence it would be
numbered in (the sheet's, or its period's when per-period numbering is on), and its old number is
never used again; a draft, having no number, gets none. CLAIM_REASSIGNED carries the new number.
Moving claims together follows the same rule, in list order.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Moving a claim to another person now gives it a new number, and all 4 acceptance tests pass (`PORT=3917 bin/e2e`).

**What changed**
- **Single reassign** (`ClaimService.reassign`): a claim that already has a number gets the next one in its sequence — the sheet's, or its period's when per-period numbering is on. It uses the same counter as opening a claim, so the old number is never handed out again. A draft still has no number. `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` now shows the new number, and the doc comment says so.
- **Bulk reassign** (`BulkMoveService.reassign`): claims are now moved one at a time **in the order they were ticked**, which is the order the page already sends them. Bulk open and bulk settle still use the old order: people in the order they were added, then each person's claims newest first.

**Decision for you:** the test only passed once I changed the bulk-reassign order, which goes against a literal reading of "in list order". In the test, both selected claims belong to Ben when the bulk reassign runs. The screen's newest-first order would move the 5.00 claim first. The expected audit file wants the 10.00 claim first, which is the order they were ticked. Using tick order was the simplest rule that matches the test. The other rule that fits — a claim moved to someone counts as their newest — would also change how the screen orders claims, so I didn't do it. If you meant something else, this is the part to revisit.

**Running the tests**
- Port 3000 was already taken by another process on this machine, so the first runs hit the wrong app. Pass a different `PORT` to `bin/e2e`.
- One run failed while filling in the add-person form during setup, which I didn't touch. The test passed in the runs either side of it, so I take it to be flaky.
